newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease few pct on Dow, outlook mixed.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease few pct on Dow, outlook mixed.

text.p: Russian shares took their cue from Wall Street's dismal Friday performance and fell a few percent in the first hour of trade on Monday though traders were mixed as to where the market would close.

Brunswick's Martin Diggle said the market could recover if Wall Street opened unchanged. A Moscow trader predicted Russia would end down 3-4 percent for the day. "It will be across the board -- all the way from LUKoil to something like Chelyab Svyazinform."
The Russian Trading System 21-share index had inched down about half a percent to 561.28 at 0800 GMT after opening at 563.45, almost unchanged from Friday's closing 563.14.

LUKoil LKOH.RTS oil company had lost about 2.5 percent, trading steadily near $27.15 at 0828 GMT, down from $27.86 at the close on Friday. Telecom Chelyab Svyazinform SVIC.RTS had not traded since Thursday's $77.50 close.
Many shares were fluctuating a few percentage points below Friday's close after an hour and a half of trade.

"After Friday's Dow and an upcoming possible rate hike in the States, markets globally are taking a breather," a Moscow trader said, adding operators tended to exaggerate fundamental U.S.-Russia correlation in their trading policy.
The Dow Jones lost more than 330 points last week in its worst ever point performance and the index fell more than three percent on Friday.
The U.S. Federal Reserve will consider interest rate policy on Tuesday.
Dealers said Russian activity continued to support the market and Diggle said domestic operators accounted for up to 70 percent of deals.
"Domestic Russian buying is much less sensitive to global events than many other emerging markets," he said. "Prices are being marked down because people don't want to be hit."
He said volumes were relatively low and few Westerners were selling.
